name: Lena Osborne
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember the house where scales replaced the supper bell.” On Saturday, near the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, Lena can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I bought it so my son would come home to practice. I didn't measure the stairs or ask him.
appearance: Lena has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Look for a dark undercut with a longer wave on top. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a gray fisher's sweater with a pen clipped inside the neckline. In conversation Lena leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations.
personality: Lena can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Lena can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.
agenda: To invite the son to choose whether to come back and play.
family: Keir Pierce is Lena’s half-sibling. Lena brings a spare shopping bag. Keir chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The uniform money*, Keir says, “I caused the leak moving a hose to mop the floor.”
connections: Alexei Taylor (ground-floor host). The owner and the ground-floor tenant have to agree on lessons as well as rent.
